kaps_punt: Kindermishandeling: Verskillende vorme van kindermishandeling: fisies en emosioneel; Effek van mishandeling op persoonlike gesondheid; Strategiee om mishandeling te hanteer; en Waar om hulp te vind en mishandeling aan te meld.

items.bewering: Party grootmense maak 'n kind aspris seer. Ander behandel 'n kind so sleg dat dit hom skade doen. Albei is kindermishandeling.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s1 definition of 'abuse': 'any form of harm or ill-treatment deliberately inflicted on a child', including assault and exposing a child to behaviour that may harm it psychologically or emotionally (justice.gov.za/legislation/acts/2005-038 childrensact.pdf; saflii.org/za/legis/consol_act/ca2005104). Volledig nagegaan in hierdie rondte; geen inligting oor wat verander het nie.

items.bewering: 'n Grootmens of 'n ander kind kan dit doen.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s1: the definition of 'abuse' expressly includes 'bullying by another child' (justice.gov.za; saflii.org).

items.bewering: Mishandeling gebeur nooit per ongeluk nie en lyk nie altyd dieselfde nie.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s1: abuse is harm 'deliberately inflicted', and the definition lists several distinct forms. International definitions likewise describe physical abuse as non-accidental injury (childhelphotline.org/what-is-abuse/physical-abuse).

items.bewering: Fisiese mishandeling is wanneer iemand 'n kind se liggaam aspris seermaak, soos om hom te slaan, skop, brand of gooi.
items.bron: NSPCC, physical abuse (nspcc.org.uk/what-is-child-abuse/types-of-abuse/physical-abuse) and Childhelp (childhelphotline.org/what-is-abuse/physical-abuse): hitting, kicking, burning and throwing are all listed; Children's Act s1 'assaulting a child or inflicting any other form of deliberate injury'.

items.bewering: Dit los soms 'n merk.
items.bron: Childhelp and American SPCC (americanspcc.org/physical-child-abuse): bruises, welts and burns are listed as possible signs, not invariable ones, so 'soms' is correct.

items.bewering: Emosionele mishandeling gebeur met woorde en dade. Oor en oor skel iemand 'n kind uit, maak hom klein of bang, of laat hom voel hy is nie gewens nie.
items.bron: Mayo Clinic, child abuse (mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/child-abuse/symptoms-causes/syc-20370864): continually belittling or berating, rejecting; Childhelp, emotional abuse (childhelphotline.org/what-is-abuse/emotional-abuse): patterns that make a child feel unwanted, shaming, terrorizing. NSPCC Learning (learning.nspcc.org.uk/child-abuse-and-neglect/emotional-abuse) describes it as persistent.

items.bewering: Dit los geen merk op die liggaam nie. Dit is steeds mishandeling en doen skade.
items.bron: Mayo Clinic and Childhelp: emotional abuse typically has no outward physical signs but causes psychological harm; Children's Act s1 includes behaviour that harms a child psychologically or emotionally as abuse.

items.bewering: Mishandeling raak 'n kind se gesondheid en nie net sy liggaam nie.
items.bron: Mayo Clinic, child abuse: emotional and behavioural consequences (anxiety, depression, withdrawal) alongside physical ones.

items.bewering: Sommige kinders wat mishandel word slaap sleg of eet sleg. Party voel baie bang en ander voel kwaad vir mense om hulle. Party sukkel om by die skool te konsentreer of bly van ander kinders af weg.
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital, '9 signs of child abuse and neglect' (nationwidechildrens.org/family-resources-education/700childrens/2017/04/recognizing-signs-of-child-abuse-and-neglect): sleep problems and nightmares, changes in eating, difficulty concentrating; Mayo Clinic: fear, anxiety, aggression, withdrawal from friends. The quantifiers 'sommige' and 'party' are correctly narrow.

items.bewering: Nie een van hierdie tekens beteken op sy eie dat 'n kind mishandel word nie.
items.bron: Mayo Clinic, child abuse: these signs are warning signs and can have other causes. Sound, and it protects against a learner self-diagnosing or accusing.

items.bewering: Mishandeling is nooit die kind se skuld nie. Dit bly waar al sê die grootmens die kind het dit verdien. Dit bly waar al was die kind stout of ongehoorsaam.
items.blok: Dit is nooit die kind se skuld nie
items.bron: Nemours KidsHealth, 'Abuse: what kids need to know' (kidshealth.org): 'Abuse is never your fault and you don't deserve it'; Childhelp, safe vs unsafe secrets. Consistent with SA law, which since Freedom of Religion SA v Minister of Justice (ConCourt 2019) gives no chastisement defence for hitting a child at home.

items.bewering: 'n Grootmens wat 'n kind seermaak het self so gekies.
items.blok: Dit is nooit die kind se skuld nie
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s1: abuse is harm 'deliberately inflicted'; the responsibility lies with the one who inflicts it (KidsHealth: the abuse is the fault of the abuser).

items.bewering: Om die mishandeling stop te sit is die werk van ander grootmense en nie die kind s'n nie.
items.blok: Dit is nooit die kind se skuld nie
items.bron: Childline South Africa, educators' pages (childlinesa.org.za/educators/for-educators/child-protection-at-school/procedures-for-reporting-abuse): educators must report and the matter goes to social workers and SAPS child protection officers; Children's Act s110 places the reporting duty on adults. KidsHealth: keep telling 'until an adult gets help and the abuse stops'.

items.bewering: Die belangrikste is om dit te vertel.
items.blok: Vertel dit vir iemand wat jy vertrou
items.bron: Nemours KidsHealth (kidshealth.org, 'Abuse: what kids need to know'): 'the bravest and most important thing you can do is tell someone you trust'. Childline South Africa gives the same central advice (tell an adult who will listen and do something about it). The superlative is the established framing in child-protection guidance, and the block goes on to put getting to safety first when it is not safe, so it does not compete with safety.

items.bewering: Kies 'n volwassene wat jy vertrou soos 'n onderwyser of ouma. As daardie een nie luister of help nie, vertel 'n ander volwassene wat jy vertrou. Hou aan tot iemand help.
items.blok: Vertel dit vir iemand wat jy vertrou
items.bron: Childline South Africa: 'Tell an adult who will listen and do something about it. Keep telling people you trust ... until someone listens' (childlinesa.org.za); Nemours KidsHealth teens page: 'if you talk to someone who is not helpful, don't give up and keep telling'.

items.bewering: 'n Geheim wat jou bang maak is nie 'n geheim wat jy hoef te hou nie.
items.blok: Vertel dit vir iemand wat jy vertrou
items.bron: Childhelp, 'Safe vs unsafe secrets' (childhelp.org/safe-vs-unsafe-secrets-how-to-talk-to-kids-about-the-difference): unsafe secrets are those that make a child feel scared, unhappy or hurt, and should be told to a trusted adult; KidsHealth: never keep it a secret even if told something bad will happen.

items.bewering: As dit veilig is, mag jy 'Nee' sê en weggaan, ook vir 'n grootmens by die huis. Is dit nie veilig nie, gaan na 'n veilige plek of ander mense.
items.blok: Vertel dit vir iemand wat jy vertrou
items.bron: National Center for Missing and Exploited Children 'No, Go, Tell' model, as summarised by the US Department of Education, 'Personal safety for children: a guide for parents' (ed.gov/sites/ed/files/parents/academic/involve/safety/personal_safety.pdf) and Zero Abuse Project (zeroabuseproject.org/victim-assistance/jwrc/personal-safety): say no, get away, tell. The lesson's 'as dit veilig is' condition is the right safeguard. It does not tell a child to resist physically.

items.bewering: Kon jy nie nee sê of wegkom nie, het jy niks verkeerd gedoen nie. Vertel daarna altyd iemand.
items.blok: Vertel dit vir iemand wat jy vertrou
items.bron: Nemours KidsHealth: abuse is never the child's fault; personal-safety guidance (Zero Abuse Project) stresses telling afterwards whatever happened. The sentence correctly stops 'say no and go' being read as a duty the child failed.

items.bewering: Moenie later teruggaan om die persoon daaroor aan te spreek of te stry nie, grootmens of kind. Om dit verder te neem is die werk van grootmense soos onderwysers, maatskaplike werkers en die polisie.
items.blok: Vertel dit vir iemand wat jy vertrou
items.bron: OVC Help Series (ovc.ojp.gov) and Childhelp's disclosure guide (childhelp.org): 'do not confront the alleged perpetrator', since confronting may cause more harm to the child; Childline South Africa educators' page: school staff must not investigate and must refer to a social worker or the SAPS child protection officer. These sources address adults; the advice holds a fortiori for a child and contradicts nothing.

items.bewering: Kindermishandeling is teen die wet in Suid-Afrika.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s305(3): a parent, guardian or care-giver who abuses or deliberately neglects a child is guilty of an offence (lawlibrary.org.za/akn/za/act/2005/38 s305); assault of a child by anyone is a crime under common law.

items.bewering: Die wet sê onderwysers en susters by die kliniek moet dit aanmeld as hulle glo 'n kind is so mishandel dat hy beseer is.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s110(1): teachers and nurses are among the listed professionals who must report when they conclude on reasonable grounds that a child 'has been abused in a manner causing physical injury, sexually abused or deliberately neglected', to a designated child protection organisation, the provincial Department of Social Development or a police official (Department of Health, 'Mandatory reporting in terms of the Children's Act', knowledgehub.health.gov.za; SciELO SA, 'Mandatory reporting of child abuse in South Africa: legislation explored'). The lesson's sentence is accurate for the physical-abuse limb, which is the one this lesson teaches. It does not say 'only', and it correctly does not claim a legal duty to report emotional abuse, which s110 does not impose. Sexual abuse and neglect, which also trigger the duty, fall outside the lesson and their omission creates no false contrast.

items.bewering: Jy kan Childline self gratis bel, dag en nag.
items.bron: Childline South Africa (childlinesa.org.za): 'Call us 24/7 - we are free from all networks'; toll-free number 116, a national 24-hour telephone counselling service for children under 18 (findahelpline.com/organizations/childline-south-africa; Vuk'uzenzele, 'Children can call 116 for help', vukuzenzele.gov.za).

items.bewering: Childline hou wat jy vertel privaat, behalwe as hulle dink jy is in gevaar of meer hulp nodig het.
items.bron: Childline South Africa confidentiality policy (childlinesa.org.za/about/how-we-help/online-counselling): 'Confidentiality means not telling anyone else about what you've said unless we feel you are in danger or may need further help.' The lesson's wording matches that condition closely.

items.bewering: Dan kan hulle 'n maatskaplike werker of die polisie inbring.
items.bron: Vuk'uzenzele (government publication), 'Children can call 116 for help': 'If necessary, Childline will refer them to the police and/or a social worker at the Department of Social Development.'

items.bewering: 'n Volwassene kan ook help om te bel.
items.bron: Vuk'uzenzele: 'By dialing 116, children and adults can receive help with problems facing children'; Childline South Africa's service is also open to adults with concerns about children. True as written. The sentence comes after the child is told she can phone herself, so it is not a condition of calling.

items.bewering: Jy kan ook vertel as dit met 'n ander kind gebeur.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s110(2): any person who believes on reasonable grounds that a child is abused may report it (Department of Health, mandatory reporting document; SciELO SA article: ordinary citizens may report but are not compelled); Vuk'uzenzele, 'Child protection is everyone's business'.

items.bewering: 'n Onderwyser of die skoolhoof by jou skool; 'n maatskaplike werker wat kinders en gesinne help; 'n suster by die kliniek; die polisie by die naaste polisiestasie.
items.bron: Childline South Africa educators' page: reports go to a social worker at a child protection organisation or the Department of Social Development, or to the SAPS child protection officer; Children's Act s110: teachers and nurses are mandatory reporters and a police official is a lawful recipient of a report.

items.bewering: Childline se hulplyn wat jy self gratis kan bel, dag en nag
items.bron: Childline South Africa (childlinesa.org.za): free from all networks, 24/7, on 116. Same claim as in 'Waar hulp te kry is'.

items.bewering: kindermishandeling: Wanneer 'n grootmens of 'n ander kind 'n kind aspris skade doen.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s1: harm 'deliberately inflicted on a child', including 'bullying by another child'. Read alone, the entry still holds, since the Act covers deliberate harm by another child as well as by an adult.

items.bewering: fisiese mishandeling: Wanneer iemand 'n kind se liggaam aspris seermaak.
items.bron: Children's Act s1 ('assaulting a child or inflicting any other form of deliberate injury'); NSPCC, physical abuse.

items.bewering: emosionele mishandeling: Wanneer iemand 'n kind oor en oor met woorde of dade afbreek.
items.bron: NSPCC Learning, emotional abuse (persistent emotional maltreatment); Mayo Clinic ('continually belittling or berating'). The 'oor en oor' (repeatedly) element matches the standard definitions.

items.bewering: maatskaplike werker: Iemand wat opgelei is om mense te help met probleme in hulle lewe, ook kinders en gesinne.
items.bron: In South Africa social work is a trained, registered profession (Social Service Professions Act 110 of 1978; SACSSP), and child protection is part of the work: Childline South Africa educators' page refers reports to social workers at child protection organisations and the Department of Social Development.

items.bewering: Childline: 'n Diens wat kinders kan bel wanneer hulle hulp nodig het.
items.bron: Childline South Africa (childlinesa.org.za; Wikipedia 'Childline South Africa'): national telephone counselling helpline for children, 116.

items.bewering: aanmeld: Om vir die regte mense te gaan se wat gebeur het.
items.bron: Children's Act s110: a report is made to a designated child protection organisation, the provincial Department of Social Development or a police official, i.e. the proper authorities. The everyday sense of 'aanmeld' (to report to the proper authority) fits.

opsomming: Alle 34 bewerings is nagegaan en bevestig, met geen weerspreek of onseker nie: die veiligheidsraad (vertel, hou aan vertel, sê nee en gaan weg slegs as dit veilig is, moenie die persoon aanspreek nie) stem ooreen met erkende kinderbeskermingsriglyne; die wetsbewering stem ooreen met artikel 110 van die Kinderwet (onderwysers en verpleegsters moet aanmeld wanneer mishandeling tot 'n fisiese besering gelei het, en die les beweer tereg geen plig om emosionele mishandeling aan te meld nie); en die Childline-bewerings (gratis, dag en nag, privaat behalwe as die kind in gevaar is of meer hulp nodig het, verwysing na 'n maatskaplike werker of die polisie) stem ooreen met Childline se eie bewoording en die regering se Vuk'uzenzele.
